svg.title: A Halloween evening that welcomes everyone

text.tspan: Everyday English - C2 - 2026/10/26 - 01 - Essay
A costume creates a playful Halloween character.
Pexels · 29225548
A Halloween evening that welcomes everyone
To prepare a Halloween evening is to negotiate a familiar but frequently obscured relationship between intentional design and the contingencies of shared
experience. The question is not whether arrangements are desirable, but what authority they should acquire. A credible position supports preparation while
withholding the assumption that procedural coherence is equivalent to human value.
There is a substantive case for structure: planning the route and the costumes helps everyone stay comfortable. Here, we check that costumes allow
clear vision and choose a well-lit route. The arrangement earns its legitimacy through the specific difficulty it alleviates, not through its conformity to an
abstract ideal of order. Its success is consequently conditional. Once the intervention demands more attention than the obstacle it removes, the original
justification begins to unravel.
An assessment confined to that practical benefit would nevertheless be incomplete, since clear choices make sharing treats more considerate. In
concrete terms, we keep ingredient information available and offer a non-food option. This introduces a problem of perspective: whose convenience
supplies the standard against which improvement is measured? An apparently neutral procedure may privilege the preferences of its designer.
Attentiveness to others makes that asymmetry visible and creates grounds for revision.
What emerges is a qualified defence of planning, rather than a celebration of either control or spontaneity. Arrangements can sustain an experience
without exhausting its meaning. Their authority should remain answerable to the people and circumstances they affect; otherwise, a means of making life
more habitable risks becoming the criterion to which life must conform.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a focused main idea. Develop one supporting reason in each body paragraph, with a concrete example. Conclude by
connecting the two reasons without introducing a new argument. Use the structure as a model; write about an experience of your own.
What two reasons support the main idea? Explain one example. (Model: The two reasons are that planning the route and the costumes helps everyone
stay comfortable and that clear choices make sharing treats more considerate. One example is that we check that costumes allow clear vision and
choose a well-lit route.)
